title: Dubai trials new transport system with driverless pods that operate away from traffic
source_used: Khaleej Times (read in full from the pre-fetched text)
key_facts: Dubai's Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) launched a four-week trial of the Dubai Glydways automated transit system at Bluewaters on Sunday 11 Oct 2026.
Driverless electric pods carry four to six passengers at up to 50 km/h on dedicated, narrow guideways, at ground level or elevated, and run on demand without fixed timetables.
Each pod has 20 high-resolution LiDAR sensors plus radar and cameras; RTA says more than 10 vehicles can be linked less than a second apart.
RTA says the system can carry more than 20,000 passengers per hour in each direction and costs up to 90 per cent less to build and up to 70 per cent less to run than comparable transport systems.
RTA Director General Mattar Al Tayer took a five-minute ride; Glydways founder and co-CEO Mark Seeger and co-CEO Blake Barber attended.
The trial will assess safety, reliability, passenger experience, journey times and ease of use, and will help RTA judge readiness for wider use.
The trial follows a cooperation agreement between RTA and Glydways and is run with Dubai Holding.
quote_evidence: The Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) launched a four-week trial of the Dubai Glydways automated transit system at Bluewaters on Sunday, October 11.
It also offers potential cost savings, with capital costs up to 90 per cent lower and operating costs up to 70 per cent lower than comparable transport systems, according to the authority.
The four-week trial at Bluewaters will assess how the autonomous vehicles perform in an operational environment, with particular attention to safety, reliability and passenger experience.
why_it_matters_hint: Dubai's transport authority is testing small driverless pods on their own tracks as a possible alternative to buses and rail.
notes: Launch is an official RTA event; the capacity and cost figures are RTA's claims and the trial is meant to test them.
